subject: Your Scam-Proof Checklist is here
preheader: Start with the 10-minute part. It blocks the scams that cost the most.
goal: Deliver the checklist, get one action done tonight, ask for a reply
html:
Start with the 10-minute part. It blocks the scams that cost the most.

Hi,

Here's your checklist: download The Scam-Proof Checklist (PDF). Two pages, printable.

If you only do one thing from it tonight, make it the top section: 10 minutes, three free settings.

  • Freeze your credit at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion (free by law, doesn't touch your score)
  • Pick a family safe word and say it out loud at dinner, not by text
  • Turn on transaction alerts for every bank account and card

Those three quietly block the scams that cost people the most: new accounts opened in your name, the "I'm in trouble, send money" call, and fraud that runs for weeks before anyone notices.

Over the next two weeks I'll send you six short emails, one scam pattern each, with the tell that gives it away and what to do. No panic, no "you've been hacked" subject lines.

One favour: hit reply and tell me the weirdest scam text or call you've had this year. I read every reply, and the best ones become videos (with every personal detail removed).

The Scam Decoded team

subject: Every scam I've ever decoded has the same 3 tells
preheader: Rush, secrecy, and a strange way to pay. See two, stop.
goal: Teach the universal pattern; introduce the free scam checker
html:
Rush, secrecy, and a strange way to pay. See two, stop.

Hi,

Toll texts, fake bank calls, puppy sellers, "your computer is infected". The stories change every week. Underneath, almost every scam has the same three parts:

  1. Rush. A deadline, a countdown, "today only", "within 2 hours". Urgency stops you from checking.
  2. Secrecy. "Don't tell your bank." "Keep this between us." "Leave the dating app and text me." Secrecy stops anyone else from checking.
  3. A strange way to pay. Gift cards, wire transfers, crypto, a Bitcoin ATM, a payment app to a stranger, cash to a courier. These are fast and nearly impossible to reverse.

See two of the three? Stop. Hang up, close the tab, and check on your own: call back on a number you look up yourself, or type the website in yourself.

Got a message right now you're not sure about? Paste it into our free scam checker. It looks for look-alike links, payment demands and the patterns behind toll, delivery, bank and job scams. It's not perfect, so when in doubt, call the company on a number you found yourself.

Tomorrow-ish: the free 10-minute move that blocks most identity theft.

The Scam Decoded team

subject: $0 and 10 minutes (the move most people still haven't made)
preheader: A credit freeze is free, doesn't hurt your score, and blocks new-account fraud.
goal: Walk through the credit freeze; reinforce the checklist
html:
A credit freeze is free, doesn't hurt your score, and blocks new-account fraud.

Hi,

The identity theft that costs real money is usually a thief opening a new account in your name: a credit card, a phone plan, a loan. A credit freeze stops that, because lenders can't pull your report.

Here's the whole thing:

  1. Go to Equifax, Experian and TransUnion directly. Type the addresses yourself; don't click ads.
  2. Make an account at each one and switch the freeze on.
  3. Save the three logins somewhere safe (a password manager is ideal).
  4. Applying for a loan or card later? Ask the lender which bureau it uses and lift only that one, for a day or two.

What it doesn't do: hurt your credit score, stop your existing cards working, or cost anything. Freezes and lifts are free by federal law.

Bonus round: parents can freeze a child's credit too (under 16), and two smaller agencies, Innovis and ChexSystems, offer free freezes as well.

If you do one thing this week, do this. Then do your parents'.

The Scam Decoded team

P.S. Some companies sell "identity protection". It can be useful for monitoring and recovery help, but the freeze itself is free, and it's the part that actually blocks new accounts.

subject: The call that sounds exactly like your grandson
preheader: Voices can be cloned now. One word fixes it.
goal: Voice clone / family emergency scam; set up the safe word; soft kit mention
html:
Voices can be cloned now. One word fixes it.

Hi,

The call comes late in the evening. It's your grandson's voice, crying. He's been in an accident, he's at the police station, please don't tell Mom. Then a "lawyer" takes the phone and asks for bail money, today, in cash or gift cards.

This scam is old. What's new is that scammers can clone a voice from a short clip posted online. So "it sounded exactly like him" isn't proof anymore. The FBI now recommends families agree on a secret word or phrase for exactly this.

Set it up this week:

  • Pick a word or phrase that isn't findable online (not a pet's name, street or school).
  • Say it out loud. Don't text it or post it.
  • The rule: anyone calling in a panic about money has to say it. No word, or they dodge the question? Hang up and call that person back on the number you already have.

The hardest part isn't picking the word. It's getting the whole family, especially parents and grandparents, to agree on the rules before a scary call happens. That's why I made a printable family plan. It's in the next email, if you want it.

The Scam Decoded team

subject: If it happens: the first 60 minutes, in order
preheader: Speed matters more than shame. Save this one.
goal: Recovery steps; build trust; checker link
html:
Speed matters more than shame. Save this one.

Hi,

Save this email. I hope you never need it.

It happens to careful, smart people every day. These are professionals. Shame is what scammers count on to stop you acting, and speed matters more than anything: money can sometimes be stopped if you move fast (not always).

In order:

  1. Call your bank or card issuer on the number on the back of your card. Say "I've been scammed." Ask them to stop or reverse the payment and lock the card.
  2. Call where the money went. Gift card? Call the card company on the number on the card. Payment app or wire? Contact them directly.
  3. Change passwords, email first, from a device the scammer never touched. If you gave someone remote access, disconnect that computer from the internet first.
  4. Freeze your credit if you shared your Social Security number or ID.
  5. Report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov, and at IdentityTheft.gov if your identity was used (it builds you a recovery plan).
  6. Write everything down: names, numbers, dates, amounts, how you paid.

And one warning: anyone who contacts you offering to recover your money for a fee is very likely the next scammer.

Not sure whether something is a scam in the first place? Run it through the free checker before you reply or pay.

The Scam Decoded team

P.S. The kit's "It happened" plan is this list as a fill-in sheet, with an incident log your bank and the police will ask for. It's in The Family Scam-Proofing Kit, $9.

preheader: Honest answers about the kit, then one scam alert a week.
goal: Objections + last pitch; hand off to the weekly scam alert
html:
Honest answers about the kit, then one scam alert a week.

Hi,

Two weeks in. Quick recap, then the questions people ask before getting the kit.

The recap: freeze your credit (free), set a family safe word, call back on numbers you look up yourself, and never pay anyone who contacted you with gift cards, wires, crypto or a payment app.

"Will my parents actually use it?" The kit is designed for the moment they're scared, not for reading cover to cover. The fridge card and wallet cards are what get used. The family meeting script is how you get them to agree to it without a lecture.

"Isn't this all free online?" Yes, most of the facts are, and these emails gave you the core of it. The kit saves you turning it into a plan your family will follow: the trackers, the cards, the script.

"Is $9 worth it?" A single panicked gift card or wire payment is often hundreds of dollars. If the kit stops one, it paid for itself. And there's a 14-day refund if it doesn't help.

Get the Family Scam-Proofing Kit for $9 →
